candidates.attacker_control: The HTTP request target. For keyword handlers the raw path is taken from the server request and decoded by URI.getPath() (WebContextBase.path()); percent-encoded dot/slash sequences such as /static/..%2f..%2fapplication.yml, or literal ../ where the concrete server does not normalize, become '../..' segments in the value handed to StaticMappings.find(). No authentication, cookies/herders, or application routes are needed: XPluginImp registers the handler with handler().prev(...) so it runs before the router/filter chain.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: ClassPathStaticRepository's normal (non-debug) branch delegates to ClassLoader.getResource(location+relativePath), where the JDK URLClassPath FileLoader rejects escapes above the classpath base and jar lookups only match literal entry names - so the default classpath repository is not exploitable; servlet-container adapters (Tomcat/Jetty/Undertow through solon-web-servlet*) receive already-normalized paths; static-file handling requires a suffix (extension) so extension-less files such as /etc/passwd are not served; and the finding depends on a file-backed mapping (or debug mode) being configured, which is not the out-of-the-box default. No `..`/canonical check was found anywhere (searches for normalize()/contains("..")/getCanonicalPath in the request-to-file path returned nothing relevant), and the handler is inserted before the router, so app-level filters cannot sanitize it.
candidates.impact: Disclosure of arbitrary readable files whose path can be reached from the configured static root and whose last path segment contains a dot (application.yml/.properties/.xml/.json/.log/.class/.key/.conf, source files, etc.) - i.e., configuration, credentials and source disclosure outside the web root. The gzip/brotli lookups (path + '.gz'/'.br') share the same root cause. No write/execution is provided by this handler itself.
candidates.prerequisites: The solon-web-staticfiles plugin is on the classpath (solon.staticfiles.enable and SolonApp.enableStaticfiles default to true) and at least one mapping backed by a file-system repository exists (StaticMappings.add(...) programmatic usage, or solon.staticfiles.mappings with a non-classpath repository), or the app runs in debug mode so ClassPathStaticRepository resolves to a file directory. Request must be GET and the targeted file name must contain an extension after its last '/' (findByExtName), since Utils.mime() falls back to application/octet-stream for any suffix, any existing dotted file can be fetched. Non-servlet boot adapters (jdkhttp/jlhttp/smarthttp wrappers that pass the raw request URI) are the clearest exposure; servlet containers normalize/reject encoded traversal.
candidates.root_cause: The static-file pipeline never normalizes or validates dot-segments. StaticResourceHandler.handle() uses ctx.pathNew() (the URL-decoded request path, produced from URI.getPath() in WebContextBase.path()) as the resource path; StaticMappings.find() only checks the configured prefix and passes the remainder as relativePath; FileStaticRepository.find(), ExtendStaticRepository.find() and ClassPathStaticRepository.find() (debug/file branch) then do `new File(baseDir, relativePath)` and, if the file exists, return it as a file: URL that OutputUtils streams back. No canonical-path containment check, `..` rejection, or allowlist exists anywhere in the chain.
candidates.title: Path traversal in solon.web.staticfiles allows reading files outside the configured static directory
candidates.trace: Context.pathNew() -> WebContextBase.path(): url() => URI.create() then uri().getPath() (decoded), only '//' is collapsed -> StaticResourceHandler.handle(): path = ctx.pathNew(); suffix=mime lookup; StaticMappings.find(path) -> StaticMappings.find(): path.startsWith(prefix) then repository.find(path.substring(prefix.length())) -> FileStaticRepository.find(): new File(location, relativePath); file.exists() -> return file.toURI().toURL() -> StaticResourceHandler: OutputUtils.global().outputFile(ctx, resUri, conentType, ...) writes the file bytes to the response.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. External HTTP server libraries (smart-http, jlhttp, vertx) are not in the tree, so whether each preserves the raw request target (and therefore allows decoded `..`) was only reasoned from the Solon wrapper code (e.g. JdkHttpContext.url(), JlHttpContext.url(), SmHttpContext.url() -> URI.create(url()).getPath()); this must be confirmed per adapter. The exact set of deploy configurations using FileStaticRepository in the wild is unknown, and the mime/extension gate limits which files are retrievable.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Path Traversal / CWE-552 Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties

coverage_summary: Reviewed the static-file module end to end (handler, mappings, locations, all three repository types, config/plugin wiring), the context/path pipeline (Context, WebContextBase, HandlerPipeline, ContextPathFilter) and the boot adapters' url()/uri() implementations (jdkhttp, jlhttp, smarthttp, servlet, vertx wrappers), plus targeted sweeps of session handling, IpUtil, cors, auth, validation, faas-luffy, data cache serializers, config-yaml/snakeyaml, vault, view renderers, docs/demo modules, netty hatch modules, and update logs. The P1 index covers 2,484 of 2,493 source files (9 omitted/likely binary) and parsed 429 files for symbols; it reports no control-flow/data-flow support, 22,884 unresolved calls, and annotation/DI only as name-based candidates - none of its facts or edges were treated as vulnerability proof. Not every one of the 2,493 files was read line-by-line; areas with no plausible remote input were sampled rather than exhaustively audited.
limitations: No code was executed, built, or scanned; no HTTP server was started, so the traversal is a source-level lead, not a runtime-confirmed exploit.

Exploitability depends on deployment configuration (file-backed static mapping or debug mode) and on the concrete HTTP adapter preserving encoded/literal dot-segments - jdkhttp/jlhttp/smarthttp wrappers were read, but the third-party server libraries themselves are not in the snapshot.
The findByExtName/mime gate means only files whose last path segment contains an extension can be served, which narrows but does not eliminate the impact.
The P1 relation index omits 9 files and has no semantic resolution; conclusions about call reachability are based on source reading, not index edges alone.
The repository is large (2,493 files); non-web utility, cloud, scheduling, native/AOT and tooling modules were only sampled, so additional issues may exist that are not mentioned here.

rejected_leads.lead: Unsafe deserialization defaults in the serialization plugins: JacksonActionExecutor.newMapper() enables activateDefaultTypingAsProperty(..., JAVA_LANG_OBJECT, "@type") with the laissez-faire default PolymorphicTypeValidator and setVisibility(ALL, ANY) for request bodies; KryoBytesSerializer sets registrationRequired=false and readClassAndObject(); HessianBytesSerializer calls readObject() on the body; Fury uses AllowListChecker with CheckLevel.WARN so the blacklist only logs.
rejected_leads.reason: All are real risks (CWE-502) but they live in opt-in serialization plugins, require a body-bound action plus (for RCE) a gadget on the deployment classpath, and the typed behavior is an intentional design (SerializerNames.AT_JSON_TYPED). The Fury WARN level and the Jackson validator come from library-default examples and are a hardening/design issue rather than a single, unambiguously unintended defect; also multiple modules share the pattern, so picking one would be arbitrary.

rejected_leads.lead: solon-web-cors AbstractCross defaults: allowedOrigins="*" reflects the request Origin and allowCredentials defaults to true.
rejected_leads.reason: Insecure-default CORS behavior, but it only applies when the opt-in plugin/filter is registered and is a long-standing documented default of the project; no request path to a sensitive operation inside framework code.

rejected_leads.lead: IpUtil.getRealIp() trusts X-Real-IP / X-Forwarded-For, which feeds solon-web-stop's IP whitelist (default 127.0.0.1) and AuthRule.verifyIp().
rejected_leads.reason: The class is explicitly documented as a replaceable extension point and stop is disabled by default (solon.stop.enable=false); this is a trust-proxy configuration assumption, not a framework-internal validation defect.

rejected_leads.lead: solon-faas-luffy JtFunctionLoaderFile/Debug/Classpath build File(baseDir, path) from the request path and execute the file content according to its extension.
rejected_leads.reason: The file/debug loaders are only registered as user beans (JtRun.init installs the classpath loader); executing code files is the FaaS feature by design, and the classpath variant is protected by ClassLoader semantics. Plausible traversal-to-code-execution path, but the configuration is unusual and I did not verify it as the primary finding.

rejected_leads.lead: AesVaultCoder uses AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding with the raw password as the key and no KDF/salt.
rejected_leads.reason: Cryptographic weakness in local configuration obfuscation (solon.vault) with no remote attacker-controlled input; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: AesVaultCoder / session cookie domain check via ctx.uri().getHost().indexOf(_domain) < 0 (suffix matching can treat evildomain.com as inside domain.com).
rejected_leads.reason: The checked value (_domain) comes from application configuration, not the attacker, and the impact requires an injected cookie domain; rejected as an unconfirmed lead.

summary: Static-file serving in solon-web-staticfiles resolves the request path with no traversal validation: the handler takes the decoded request path from Context/WebContextBase, strips only a mapping prefix, and repository implementations build a java.io.File directly from the configured base directory plus that relative path. Where a file-system repository is configured (a documented, first-class setup) or the classpath repository runs in debug/file mode, an unauthenticated GET with encoded or literal dot-segments (`..`) escapes the intended static directory and returns files that exist outside it. I selected this as the single strongest candidate; the unsafe-deserialization defaults in the serialization plugins, the permissive CORS default, and header-trusting real-IP logic were reviewed but rejected as the primary finding because they are opt-in/by-design or require additional preconditions and external gadgets.
